reason: The cited evidence shows glaze layers reducing wear in NiX at 800 °C (E1) and reactive wear protection forming lubricious nanocomposites in a TiNbZrAg alloy (E2), but neither involves TiN, Y doping, or a CoCrFeNi substrate. The specific claims about Y-enhanced reactivity, TiN low-temperature hardness, and adaptive behavior across the full temperature range are not directly supported by the cited passages.
premises: Y doping enhances interfacial reactivity of TiN to promote lubricious oxide glaze formation
A glaze layer minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear at high temperature
TiN coating provides hardness to resist wear at low temperature
The combination yields an adaptive interface effective from 25 °C to 800 °C
